'''Ralph Greenberg''' (born 1944) is an American [[mathematician]] who has made contributions to [[number theory]], in particular [[Iwasawa theory]].

He was born in [[Chester, Pennsylvania]]<ref name="ias">{{cite web|url=https://library.ias.edu/files/pdfs/ar/annualreportforf1982inst.pdf|
title=The Institute for Advanced Studies, Annual Report 1981/82|publisher=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] | access-date=January 9, 2020}}</ref> and studied at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], earning a B.A. in 1966,<ref name=ias /> after which he attended [[Princeton University]], earning his [[doctorate]] in 1971 under the supervision of [[Kenkichi Iwasawa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.washington.edu/~greenber/vita.html|title=Curriculum Vita}}</ref>

Greenberg's results include a proof (joint with [[Glenn Stevens (mathematician)|Glenn Stevens]]) of the [[Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum conjecture]] as well as a formula for the derivative of a [[p-adic L-function|''p''-adic Dirichlet ''L''-function]] at <math>s=0</math> (joint with Bruce Ferrero). Greenberg is also well known for [[Greenberg's conjectures|his many conjectures]]. In his PhD thesis, he conjectured that the Iwasawa μ- and λ-invariants of the cyclotomic <math>\Z_p</math>-extension of a [[totally real field]] are zero, a conjecture that remains open as of September 2012. In the 1980s, he introduced the notion of a [[Selmer group]] for a [[p-adic Galois representation|''p''-adic Galois representation]] and generalized the [[main conjecture of Iwasawa theory|"main conjectures"]] of Iwasawa and [[Barry Mazur]] to this setting. He has since generalized this setup to present Iwasawa theory as the theory of ''p''-adic deformations of [[motive (algebraic geometry)|motives]]. He also provided an arithmetic theory of ''L''-invariants generalizing his aforementioned work with Stevens.

Greenberg was an invited speaker in [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] 2010, [[Hyderabad, India|Hyderabad]] on the topic of "''Number Theory.''"<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=2013-08-14|archive-date=2017-11-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title= List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|access-date= 2013-01-19}}</ref>

In the late 1990s and early 2000s, Greenberg publicly disputed [[NASA]] [[conspiracy theorist]] and [[pseudoscientist]] [[Richard C. Hoagland]]'s mathematical interpretations of the so-called "D&M Pyramid" and surrounding features found on the [[Cydonia (Mars)|Cydonia Planitia]] region of Mars as being conclusive signs of extraterrestrial intelligence and challenged him to a public debate. Hoagland has yet to respond.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.math.washington.edu/~greenber/update.html|title = Letter to Richard Hoagland}}</ref>
